chunks: Ali ibn Isa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qurashi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:

Indeed, Gabriel (peace be upon him) informed me of something that gladdened my eye and brought joy to my heart. He said: O Muhammad, whoever from your nation goes on an expedition in the cause of God, no raindrop from the sky or headache will afflict him except that it will count as martyrdom for him on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.جبرئيل: Gabriel (Jibril), the archangel who conveyed divine revelation to the Prophet
key_terms.سبيل الله: The cause/way of God, referring to fighting for the sake of Islam
key_terms.شهادة: Martyrdom; the rank of a witness (shahid) who is rewarded in the afterlife
key_terms.غزاة: Military expedition or battle in the way of God (ghazwa)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for suffering hardship while fighting in the cause of God in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) conveyed a glad tiding from the angel Gabriel that any hardship -- even as small as a raindrop or a headache -- endured by a Muslim soldier fighting in the cause of God will be counted as equivalent to the reward of martyrdom on the Day of Judgment. This hadith was narrated in the assembly of Sheikh al-Saduq on Friday the 22nd of Rajab, 368 AH, emphasizing the immense spiritual reward for those who endure physical suffering during jihad in the way of God.
